QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_22

question.text: Category III AIFs are taxed at:

answer.text: Fund level — the AIF pays tax on all income and gains

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Indian income-tax law, Category III AIFs do not enjoy the statutory pass-through status granted to Category I and II AIFs. Instead, the fund itself is taxed at the fund level on its income and gains (treated as business income or as the relevant character of income), and investors then receive distributions out of after-tax fund returns. Investor-level-only taxation is the pass-through treatment that applies to Cat I/II, not Cat III; neither-level taxation does not exist; and there is no flat 5% rate applicable to Cat III AIF income. The Trap: Investor-level-only is the Cat I/II pass-through model — applying it to Cat III mistakes which categories enjoy pass-through treatment. Note: A direct statement that Category III AIFs pay fund-level tax on all income and gains is not found in the NISM Series XIX-A AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook pages checked (the workbook scope is Category I/II); the framing here reflects general Indian tax-law treatment of Category III AIFs rather than a workbook citation.
